headline: LS passes Waqf Bill after a long debate
body:
The Bill was passed after several amendments moved by the Opposition were negated through division of votes; Home Minister accuses Opposition of ‘fear-mongering’ for vote bank politics; Rijiju asserts that the Bill was about ‘property’ and not ‘religion’; Opposition calls the Bill ‘unconstitutional’, with AIMIM chief symbolically ‘tearing’ a copy

**Sandeep Phukan**  
*NEW DELHI*

The Lok Sabha passed the Waqf (Amendment) Bill well past midnight on Wednesday after a marathon debate, with Home Minister Amit Shah categorically assuring the Muslim community that the new Bill does not interfere with their religious practices.

The Home Minister also accused the Opposition of **“fear-mongering”** for the sake of **“vote bank” politics**.

The debate, which started on Wednesday afternoon, went past midnight. The first clause of the Bill was passed with **288 MPs** voting in its favour. The Bill was passed after several key amendments moved by the Opposition were **negated through division of votes**.

Making an intervention during the debate, Mr. Shah made it clear that a **mutawalli** (manager/administrator of a Waqf) and the **waqif** (donor) can **only be from the Muslim community**. Non-Muslims have been included in a **Waqf Board or Council** for administrative purposes, ensuring that any donation is used for the purpose it is meant for.

> “There is an attempt to spread confusion that this law will interfere with [Muslim] religious practices and the nature of donation. Such fear-mongering is being done to create a vote bank,” he said.

He added, **“Waqf or charitable endowment is religious, not the Waqf Board or Councils.”**

> “The Narendra Modi government runs on a very clear principle that we will not bring any law for vote bank,” Mr. Shah stated.

*The stage for a fierce exchange in the House was set after Minority Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju moved the revised version of the Waqf (Amendment) Bill, the Unified Waqf Management Empowerment, Efficiency and Development Bill (UMEED).*

Asserting that the Bill was about **“property and not religion,”** Mr. Rijiju said:
> “I am from a minority myself and I can say there is no country which is safer for minorities than India.”

Opposition members, however, called the Bill **“unconstitutional”**, with All India Majlis-e-Ittehadul Muslimeen (AIMIM) chief Asaduddin Owaisi **symbolically “tearing” a copy of the Bill** in the House.

During his speech, the Home Minister said the word **‘donation’ has special importance** because donation can be done only of something that is **one’s own property** and not someone else’s. He further added that a designated official has been **authorised to ascertain the genuineness of waqf property** in case of disputes.

### *‘This is Parliament law’*

Responding to Opposition arguments that Muslims won’t accept the new law, he said:
> **“This is Parliament’s law, it is binding on everyone.”**

Taking on the Opposition, Mr. Shah claimed that they had **resorted to similar fear-mongering** during the passage of other laws such as **CAA, abrogation of Article 370, and abolition of triple talaq**.

> “Has even one Muslim person lost his citizenship because of CAA?” he asked.

Asserting that even Rashtriya Janata Dal patriarch **Lalu Prasad Yadav** wanted reform in the Waqf law, the Home Minister said the Modi government is **fulfilling Mr. Yadav’s wish**.

Stating that the Narendra Modi government **believes in the “politics of performance”**, Mr. Shah said:
> **“People blessed Modi ji with three terms as Prime Minister and the BJP will get another three more terms.”**
